mapping.strategy: WorkCount is defined in dispatch.when. Submit one 384-thread CTA per table entry; the submitted count is not an asserted residency guarantee.

schedule.strategy:
Before the main launch, a nonblocking side stream copies SeqLens, CuQ
and CuKV to pinned host buffers (4*(3*B+2) bytes); the host waits for
these copies and constructs WorkCount table entries of 48 bytes each.
Start from h ascending, b ascending, a descending. Stable-sort by N
descending exactly when every q_b>=Bq and Scatter is false.
Let CachedL2 and CachedSM be launch_impl's cached device-query results,
refreshed while CachedL2 is zero. Let ScatterBytes =
min(H*B,CachedSM if positive else 148)*max_b(k_b)*(QKDim+ValueDim).
Scatter = CachedL2>0 and 4*ScatterBytes>3*CachedL2. This is a host
locality heuristic, not a measured cache-capacity guarantee.
Upload the complete Geo table on the side stream and record table_event;
the main/current stream waits for that upload before the one main kernel.
Only allocation capacity and descriptor encodings are cached, not reused
numerical metadata. During external recording this host prefix still runs;
later execution uses the recorded binding and the table contents actually read.
Sinks has a payload only when present. LSE is stored only when ReturnLSE;
neither option changes the work set or the main kernel submission.

refill.atomic_queue:
A private global uint32 counter starts at zero when allocated.
At the start of each assigned worktile's last key iteration, request
one pop; a dedicated server atomically increments the counter and
maps its old value p to Item=worker_count+p. Publish that worktile
if Item<WorkCount, otherwise publish a terminal descriptor and stop
popping. Exactly WorkCount pops occur: WorkCount-worker_count
successful refills plus one failed pop per CTA. The pop returning
WorkCount-1 resets the counter to zero for the next ordered launch.
This queue is private scratch, separate from the supplied Workspace.

worker_assignment.exit: The terminal descriptor has been observed and all assigned work and in-flight reads and output writes have completed.

verb.latch:
Latch this CTA's preassigned Item geometry after the initialization
join, and reset M,D. The first Geometry slot is initialized from
Geo[worker_id]; the second allocated slot remains unused.
Each warp handles its consecutive 32-row group throughout this role.
verb.load: Scores(t) reads both halves of S(t) into ScoreRegisters; done releases the score read for subsequent QK slot reuse. The second-half transfer overlaps first-half masking/max work.
verb.publish:
Alpha(t) updates M and publishes all row scales before exponentiation.
P(t) copies PackedRegisters into its aliased TMEM view and completes
its writes before publication. The two-slot scale relay is safe
because QK(t+2) completion preceding its next write follows PV(t),
which already required the applicable rescale to read Alpha(t).
verb.compute: Weights(t) performs the weights rewrite after Alpha publication, retains packed P in registers and advances D.
verb.produce:
Final captures Fsum,Fmax on the last tile. For short requests,
the first row group rereads the first 32 S columns and VTile for
the tiny rewrite, storing TinyY and TinyD into the selected final
denominator. Other rows keep the main denominator. P publication remains required.

verb.latch: Latch the preassigned Item geometry after the initialization join; its four warps handle the same four consecutive 32-row groups as Softmax. Initial output credit declares the new accumulator and final-statistic storage free of old readers.
verb.rescale: Y(t) reads Alpha(t), copies all 128 previous PV columns into CorrectionRegisters before multiplying and writing them back, and publishes completion for nonfirst tiles. A group with all scales equal to one skips TMEM data traffic but still completes and publishes its rescale event.
verb.store:
Output evaluates the output rewrite using Fsum,Fmax. Ordinary rows
drain Y in four serial 32-column read/wait/convert/store chunks,
using OutputChunk registers; tiny rows read and store all TinyY
columns instead. The source returns output-state credit after its
final scratch read; this CTA has no later worktile to consume it.
Invalid query rows still execute collective reads and arithmetic;
only destination stores are masked. Write LSE exactly when present.
done covers all output writes and required source reads.

latch.meaning: Latch the preassigned Item after the initialization join. One elected issuer handles matrix operations; the warp allocates the full TMEM resource before use and frees it after the final CTA join, when all roles and their required reads and output writes have finished.

wait.meaning: QTile waits for the initial Q transfer; it does not drain unrelated operations.

verb.qk:
S(t) performs the scores rewrite from QTile and KTile(t).
It uses the same ordered tensor stream and cumulative completion
guarantee as mma.
verb.mma:
P(t)@VTile(t) performs the value_state rewrite into Y. First PV
initializes Y; later PV follows correction. Products issue in
one ordered tensor stream, and a completion notification covers
all earlier products. Earlier PV reads of an aliased P slot
finish before a later QK overwrites that slot. This ordering also
protects the tiny reread before the same S slot can recur.
PV completion releases its K/V slot. For KVSlots=3 the release
notification cycles with the three S/P slots; for KVSlots=4 it
additionally cycles with the four K/V slots, preventing parity aliasing.

verb.load:
KVSlots = 3 if Scatter, otherwise 4. QTile loads the complete
query tile into Query directly from the preassigned Geo entry
and can start during CTA initialization. KV(t) loads KTile(t)
and VTile(t); done means all bytes of both are readable.
Each Q/K transfer has a 128-channel segment and a 64-channel tail;
V has one 128-channel segment, with the padded views defined in tiles.

latch.meaning: Latch Item after issuing Q and completing the initialization join; retain its K/V base and head through all local fills.

verb.latch:
Item(w) is the assigned geometry latched into this role's registers;
N(w) denotes its positive key-tile count. Item(0) comes from the
preassigned table entry and the CTA initialization join. Reset M,D
for this worktile, but do not reset any ring or notification epoch.
Each warp handles its consecutive 32-row group throughout this role.
verb.request: Next(w) requests one refill before the last score wait. This only signals the server and does not wait for the atomic result.
verb.load: Scores(n) reads both halves of S(n) into ScoreRegisters; done releases the score read for subsequent QK slot reuse. The second-half transfer overlaps first-half masking/max work.
verb.publish:
Alpha(n) updates M and publishes all row scales before exponentiation.
P(n) copies PackedRegisters into its aliased TMEM view and completes
its writes before publication. The two-slot scale relay is safe
because the QK(n+2) completion preceding its next write follows
PV(n), which already required the applicable rescale to read Alpha(n).
verb.compute: Weights(n) performs the weights rewrite after Alpha publication, retains packed P in registers and advances D.
verb.produce:
Final(w) captures Fsum,Fmax on the last tile. For short requests,
the first row group rereads the first 32 S columns and VTile for
the tiny rewrite, storing TinyY and TinyD into the selected final
denominator. Other rows keep the main denominator. P publication remains required.
verb.wait: Next(w) observes the published next descriptor, including a failed pop; terminal descriptors end the role only after its current work has finished.

verb.latch: Latch Item(w) geometry for this role; its four warps handle the same four consecutive 32-row groups as Softmax.
verb.rescale: Y(n) reads Alpha(n), copies all 128 previous PV columns into CorrectionRegisters before multiplying and writing them back, and publishes completion for nonfirst tiles. A group with all scales equal to one skips TMEM data traffic but still completes and publishes its rescale event.
verb.store:
OutputPrefix(w) evaluates the output rewrite using Fsum,Fmax and
drains/stores the first 96 Y columns in three serial chunks.
For tiny rows it instead reads and stores all TinyY columns.
OutputTail(w) converts/stores the last 32 ordinary columns from
Tail(w) registers and then conditionally writes LSE. Invalid
query rows still execute collective reads and arithmetic; only
logical destination stores are masked. No LSE store occurs when absent.
verb.release:
OutputState(w) reads the last 32 ordinary Y columns into Tail(w).
For tiny rows the preceding prefix action has completed all scratch
reads and stores. done returns the shared Y/Fsum/Fmax/TinyY lifetime
after every row group's required reads; ordinary tail conversion,
stores and LSE write may continue after this release.
verb.wait: Next(w) consumes the next descriptor or terminal publication after this worktile's output actions.

latch.meaning: Latch Item(w). One elected issuer handles matrix operations; the warp allocates the full TMEM resource before use and frees it after the final CTA join.

wait.meaning: QTile(w) waits for the Q transfer; Next(w) consumes the next descriptor or sentinel. Neither wait drains previously issued matrix operations beyond its stated predecessors.

verb.qk:
S(n) performs the scores rewrite from the current worktile's
QTile and KTile(n). It uses the same ordered tensor stream and
cumulative completion guarantee as mma.
verb.mma:
P(n)@VTile(n) performs the value_state rewrite into Y. First PV
initializes Y; later PV follows correction. Products issue in
one ordered tensor stream, and a completion notification covers
all earlier products. Earlier PV reads of an aliased P slot
finish before a later QK overwrites that slot. This ordering also
protects the tiny reread before the same S slot can recur.
PV completion releases its K/V slot. For KVSlots=3 the release
notification cycles with the three S/P slots; for KVSlots=4 it
additionally cycles with the four K/V slots, preventing parity aliasing.

verb.load:
KVSlots = 3 if Scatter, otherwise 4. QTile(w) loads the complete
query tile into the single Query buffer; for w=0 it reads the
preassigned Geo entry directly and can start during CTA initialization.
For later work it uses the preceding Next descriptor. KV(n) loads
KTile(n) and VTile(n); done means all bytes of both are readable.
Each Q/K transfer has a 128-channel segment and a 64-channel tail;
V has one 128-channel segment, with the padded views defined in tiles.

latch.meaning: Latch Item(w) after issuing its Q transfer; retain its K/V base and head through all local fills.

wait.meaning: Next(w) waits for the server publication. A terminal descriptor performs no next-Q transfer and no next worktile; outstanding earlier fills are not implicitly reset.

verb.publish:
Next(w) executes the atomic_queue rule, copies successful geometry
or the negative tile-count terminal descriptor into Geometry, then
release-publishes it for all other roles. The terminal publication
still occurs and has a completion event; no worktile is created for
it. All consumers latch their old descriptor before that slot is
overwritten. Geometry and ring storage are allocated once per CTA;
only the queue word persists between ordered kernel executions.
